Lessons.Title: Time to the Nearest Minute
ExplanationParagraphs: Source Grade3 Unit6 Lesson9 2021 CCSS3.MD.A.1 was read from owner-device original teacher lesson.html SHA256 4ba3e65b12961e286a8a13c6f803ef427fdac3afbdfde8962451ab3acc53dc4b and preparation.html SHA256 869727695c96463381d7b15d0d9ae5ce6ab768dd172d11c7941afecfe2510cfc, with the original three student-facing text sections. A separate student PDF and original illustration pixels were not locally inspected.

Warm-up On the One Hand: an analog clock with ONLY THE HOUR HAND between 1 and 2, a little past halfway; pupils offer three estimates TOO EARLY, ABOUT RIGHT, TOO LATE. Teacher source suggests slightly later than1:30; the missing minute hand prevents one exact certified minute.

Activity1 Just a Clock on the Wall: source Lin says1:37 p.m. and Diego says1:35 p.m. Original public teacher explanation confirms LIN: long minute hand on the 37th minute mark, two ticks past the 7 (35-minute mark), not simply 35. The short hour hand is between1 and2 and advances across the hour. Sixty small marks each represent a minute.

Activity1 continues with FOUR distinct original read-an-analog-clock images A,B,C,D. Original publisher clock pixels and separate source PDF are uninspected, and local alt text does not give the hand positions. Do not fabricate A-D times: keep all four teacher-reviewed picture reading tasks until original source figures can be inspected and numerics certified.

Activity2 Show Time has FOUR ORIGINAL draw-clock targets: A 2:36 PM, B 3:18 PM, C 12:17 PM, D 9:02 PM. On each blank analog face draw the long minute hand at tick 36,18,17 or2 and the short hour hand moving partway from2,3,12 or9 as minutes pass. The text times are VERIFIED original prompts; physical drawings demand teacher inspection rather than accepting typed time alone.

Activity2 includes FIFTH original open task: draw a time of your own on the last clock, trade with partner and tell time from partner's drawn hands. Accept multiple valid student-generated times. Analog clock hands alone cannot identify AM or PM without situational context.

Source teacher preparation allows student drawing or reading differences of1–2 minutes as developmentally sufficient, but the printed original target times above remain exact. Strategies include counting printed numbers by fives and then individual minute ticks, differentiating hour and minute hands. Publisher Cool-down Times Like These, separate student PDF and source clock artwork not inspected. Tests authored but not executed; Stage D, academic approval and deployment not claimed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Analog minute precision
KeyConcepts.Definition: One full revolution of minute hand represents60 minutes.
KeyConcepts.Rule: The printed numerals count five minutes; each small tick counts one minute.
KeyConcepts.Example: Tick37 is two minute marks after7/35.

KeyConcepts.Title: Moving hour hand
KeyConcepts.Definition: Short hand moves continuously between hour numbers as minute hand advances.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Hour angle=30 degrees per hour plus0.5 degrees per minute.
KeyConcepts.Example: At2:36 hour hand is partway between2 and3.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact time versus estimate
KeyConcepts.Definition: Without a minute hand an exact minute cannot be read from original source warm-up.

KeyConcepts.Title: Hands and AM/PM
KeyConcepts.Definition: Long hand indicates minutes and short indicates hour; repeated face every12 hours.
KeyConcepts.Rule: AM or PM is context; not encoded by hand positions alone.
KeyConcepts.Example: 2:36 PM has same drawn hand geometry as2:36 AM.
